title: Free love language test: find your love language — cv.cm
description: Free love language quiz. Rate 25 statements to see how you most like to receive love: words of affirmation, quality time, gifts, acts of service or physical touch. No sign-up.
lede: Which of the five love languages speaks to you most? Rate 25 statements and see all five ranked.
about: The idea of five love languages was popularized by counselor Gary Chapman in 1992: people tend to feel loved through words of affirmation, quality time, receiving gifts, acts of service or physical touch, and partners often speak different ones.
This independent quiz was written for cv.cm. Share your ranking with a partner or friend and ask them to take it too: knowing each other's top language is the useful part.

faq.q: What are the five love languages?
faq.a: Words of affirmation, quality time, receiving gifts, acts of service, and physical touch.

faq.q: Can I have more than one love language?
faq.a: Yes. Most people have one or two that matter most and others that matter a little. The chart shows all five.

faq.q: Is the love language idea backed by research?
faq.a: Studies give it mixed support: partners who show love in many ways tend to be happier overall. It works best as a conversation starter, not a rule.
No. It is an independent quiz built on the same five categories, not affiliated with Gary Chapman or his publisher.

items: Hearing "I'm proud of you" means a lot to me.
I feel closest to someone when we spend uninterrupted time together.
A small, thoughtful gift can make my whole day.
When someone helps with my chores, I feel cared for.
A hug when I get home makes me feel loved.
I keep kind messages and read them again later.
I feel hurt when someone is on their phone while we talk.
I remember who gave me each meaningful present.
I feel loved when someone takes a task off my plate without being asked.
Holding hands makes me feel connected.
Compliments are the easiest way to brighten my mood.
A long walk or deep talk is my favorite way to bond.
I feel forgotten if a special occasion passes with no gift at all.
Actions speak louder than words for me.
I like sitting close to people I care about.
Harsh words hurt me for a long time.
Shared activities, even simple ones, mean a lot to me.
A souvenir someone brought back for me feels like love.
When someone cooks for me or fixes something, I feel valued.
A pat on the back or a touch on the arm reassures me.
I need to hear that I'm appreciated.
Cancelled plans upset me more than most things.
I like gifts that show someone was thinking of me.
I feel supported when someone helps me finish a big job.
Physical affection is important to me in a close relationship.

words.name: Words of affirmation
words.body: You feel loved through spoken and written words: compliments, encouragement, thank-yous and "I love you." Criticism hits you hard. Tell the people close to you that a short kind message matters more to you than they might think.

time.name: Quality time
time.body: You feel loved through undivided attention: real conversations, shared activities, and phones put away. Distraction and cancelled plans hurt. Ask for regular time together that both of you protect.

gifts.name: Receiving gifts
gifts.body: You feel loved through thoughtful gifts, big or small. It is not about price: it is about the proof that someone thought of you. Let people know that a small surprise means a lot.

service.name: Acts of service
service.body: You feel loved when people make your life easier: cooking, fixing, running an errand, taking over a chore. Broken promises sting. Say which specific help would mean the most to you.

touch.name: Physical touch
touch.body: You feel loved through appropriate touch: hugs, holding hands, sitting close. Physical distance can feel like emotional distance. Tell your partner how much small touches during the day matter.
